mappings.note: How image size trends as the object approaches a convex lens - qualitative lens behaviour with no numbers, so the competency's 'manipulates the position of object ... to observe image characteristics' rather than LO-3's lens formula.
Interpreting n = 2.42 as a speed reduction factor - the definition of refractive index, LO-3's middle clause.
Nature of a lens read off the sign of its power. Nearest legal code; lens power has no outcome (defect list).
Bare definition of refractive index - LO-3 is the only outcome that defines it.
Numeric reciprocal of a relative refractive index. Substitution, but LO-3 fuses definition with application so there is no separate code for it.
Straight mirror-formula substitution with the convex sign convention to find v. The answer is a number, not an object-position rule, so LO-2 rather than LO-1.
Properties of the plane-mirror image - LO-1 is the only outcome that names the plane mirror, and no formula or diagram is required.
Convex vs concave mirror compared by surface and by the images they form - image characteristics across mirror types, LO-1.
Solar furnace at the focus of a concave reflector: the converging property behind image location. No ray diagram is asked for here.
Works backwards from a magnification value (m = +6) to mirror type and image characteristics - reading the magnification formula's sign and size, which is LO-2, not the qualitative LO-1.
Object positions for two concave-mirror uses plus mirror identification from image size - all object-position-to-image-characteristic reasoning, no arithmetic.
m = -2 is turned into v = 2u and fed into the mirror formula to find u. Substitution into the finished relations, so LO-2.
Distinguishing rarer from denser by refractive index and by bending direction - the laws of refraction plus the definition of n, both in LO-3.
Pure statement of Snell's law - the 'states the laws of refraction' clause of LO-3, with no numbers and no lens.

Lens terminology (optical centre, principal axis). The competency names lens properties explicitly; LO-3 covers only laws of refraction, refractive index and the lens formula, none of which defines these terms.
Object positions that give a convex lens a virtual-enlarged or real-enlarged image - qualitative lens image characteristics, which have no outcome; the competency is the narrowest true code.
Both laws of refraction stated in full. Distinguished from the Snell's-law item only in scope; same 'states' clause of LO-3.
Equal refractive indices give no bending, and the cause of refraction is the speed change - two statements of the laws of refraction.
Definition and a numeric evaluation of n in one item; LO-3 fuses the two so a single code covers both halves.
A half-covered convex lens still forms the whole image, only fainter - a property of the lens as an optical element. No lens formula, no refractive index, so not LO-3.

The graded step is constructing rays (the undeviated ray through the optical centre, then the parallel ray) to locate the lens and its focus; the naming of the lens type rests on the competency's lens-properties clause.
Nothing is asked except completing a given lens ray diagram and reading the image nature off it - the ray-diagram outcome alone.
Textbook case of C 8.1-LO-2's 'for each position of the object': two named convex-lens object positions, diagram required, image nature read off the construction.
Ray diagram is explicitly required (C 8.1-LO-2); identifying the magnifying glass and justifying it rests on the lens-property competency, since no outcome covers a convex lens used as a magnifier.
Finding the object distance (2F = 40 cm) for a same-size lens image is the lens-position half of LO-3; the demanded ray diagram is the separate graded step.
